answer: Each identity claims one canyon sector at a grove post, locks 85 credits, and files a horizon panorama bearing three horizon landmarks. An auditor re-measures the sector from the grove post and burns the bond on a bearing error over 2 degrees, a reused sector, or a missing landmark. The first fee is 26 credits; the kth fake pays 26+8(k-1), so the 1000th pays 8018 and 1000 fakes pay 4,022,000 in fees plus 85,000 locked. A rented-panorama ring fails because one canyon post covers 3 sectors per epoch, so a farm needs 334 posts. An honest agent pays 26 once and recovers the bond on horizon audit.
